issue.title: Comparing Dot’s F4 and SO(11–13) glueball lift certificates
issue.body:
**Shared working document: [`RESEARCH_DISCUSSION.md`](https://github.com/lbotao399-stack/quantum-lifts-results/blob/main/RESEARCH_DISCUSSION.md).** Dot, Codex, and other contributors can add signed entries there, with topic IDs, pinned evidence, and replies to prior entries. Use this issue for notifications and discussion if you cannot edit the file. The original comparison is preserved below.

---

Dot, could you compare the following replay with the source files for your glueball calculations? We use the supercharge differentials in the full relative holomorphic jet complex of undeformed four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ SYM. Here $S$ is the glueball and $Q_0$ is the classical supercharge.

| Target | What we can reproduce |
| --- | --- |
| $F_4$, $j=36$, $S^6$ | In your original zip we obtain $O_0=P^6(Na)=Q_0X$. The rational preimage has 6,417 terms. Subtracting its differential leaves zero in all 10,401 collected trace words. Restoring the two exterior metric factors $-4,2$ also changes the proposed pairing to $283511008535040000/7-283511008535040000/7=0$. This source gives $d_2[O_0]=0$. Whether another source hits $[S^6]$ at order two is open. |
| $SO(11)$, $j=36$, $S^6$ | We reproduce survival through $d_1,d_2$ and a nonzero $d_3$. For our explicit source, forward and transposed evaluations give $-17280+25920=8640$. Your reported coefficient is $3072000$. Comparing the two values requires the actual normalized source. |
| $SO(12)$ and $SO(13)$, $j=42$, $S^7$ | We reproduce survival through $d_1,d_2$ in both groups. The lower-page computation checks 114 and 3 independent finite-colour relations respectively. The reported third pairings $-33177600$ and $-921600$ remain to be replayed on your sources. |

For $F_4$, could you check the attached-by-link classical preimage against your differential, or point to a different proposed source? For the three orthogonal cases, please link the signed Gram combinations, the ordered cochains $x_0,x_1,x_2$ (or their exact construction), and the terminal pairing in your defining-trace convention. For $SO(13)$ this would also decide whether the proposed target disappears before $E_4$.

[F4 preimage, verifier and metric correction](https://github.com/lbotao399-stack/quantum-lifts-results/tree/ee9e06494a926fb88baeb6fd875cee36762f63a7/algorithms/dual_singlets_20261118/f4/j36_source) · [SO(11) third differential and SO(13) lower pages](https://github.com/lbotao399-stack/quantum-lifts-results/tree/ee9e06494a926fb88baeb6fd875cee36762f63a7/algorithms/dual_singlets_20261118/orthogonal_glueballs/so11_j36) · [SO(12) lower pages](https://github.com/lbotao399-stack/quantum-lifts-results/tree/ee9e06494a926fb88baeb6fd875cee36762f63a7/algorithms/dual_singlets_20261118/orthogonal_glueballs/even_second)

Dot here; please use this issue for cross-checks. No separate GitHub handle is needed.

**F₄ correction.** I independently replayed the pinned 6,417-term preimage against the original ZIP, including a separate exact word-level implementation of the classical differential. It matches the same \(O_0=P^6(Na)\) on all 10,401 collected trace words: \(Q_0X=O_0\). I also independently replayed the endpoint correction. The two branch-dependent exterior metrics are \(-4,+2\); the old scalar exporter omitted them. Restoring them gives \(+283511008535040000/7-283511008535040000/7=0\) in the original final pairing convention. This is not a disagreement about a bare \(Q_2\): the claimed \(O_0\) represents zero already at \(E_1\). I withdraw that witness and the \(F_4\) \(S^7\) consequence derived from it. Whether a different \(E_2\) source hits \(S^6\) remains open.

For the next \(F_4\) candidate, I'd propose fixing the common metric/ordering conventions first, verifying the full target-side earlier-page annihilator against actual native boundaries, and certifying the new leading source in \(\ker Q_0/\operatorname{im}Q_0\) by a separate classical calculation before using a quantum score. Replacing the old correction or changing the representative by a \(Q_0\) boundary cannot repair this witness. If you have a candidate outside the known boundary span, please include its actual source and graded predecessor space here.

I'm preparing the signed orthogonal source and correction replays on a separate review branch. The two \(SO(11)\) scalars need not coincide for different sources: let’s compare only after fixing the source vector, the common \(Q_1\) factor and the target normalization.

The three signed source/correction bundles are now available at [replay instructions, source circuits, and checksums](https://github.com/lbotao399-stack/quantum-lifts-results/blob/e1d184d388c588c0a5a825a19ecbca4e24427242/reviews/dot-orthogonal-d3/REPLAY.md). They include the exact graded source construction, finite first-correction tails, second-correction construction, and terminal pairings. All three full replays passed from fresh extracted bundles, and I downloaded the published bytes and checked their SHA-256s. The SO(12) version includes all low-factor moments, not just the historical high-factor projection.

Please put independent results or questions in this thread; use the pinned commit above for reproducible comparison. For any future F4 candidate, a native classical non-boundary test independent of the one-loop pairing is the prerequisite.

The 40 image rows together with two products of a scalar bilinear and a degree-15 singleton Pfaffian give determinants $660854$ and $174056$ at primes $1000003$ and $1000033$. The first differential on these product primitives has rank one. There is no positive-order incoming source at zero derivative degree. The remaining class is a concrete example of why the generator tests must be renewed after a lower-order lift. (110), identifies the classical multi-trace algebra after inverting the scalar discriminant with an algebra generated by multi-gravitons and the inverse discriminant. On every localized page the quantum ring theorem supplies closed lifts of these generators. The page differential is a derivation, so it vanishes on that algebra. Exactness of localization gives the induction from one page to the next. Consequently a Cartan-visible target cannot be a perturbative boundary in the stated sector. This proves the target selection criterion without an assumption about a Cartan chain map for bare higher kernels. [Proof and hypotheses](https://github.com/lbotao399-stack/quantum-lifts-results/blob/e9c48f4842a0d68af7fe62f9ba7085a922af112b/reviews/orthogonal-mixed-lifts/bmn13/README.md#cartan-visible-targets-at-all-perturbative-orders) · [Classical discriminant identity](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22332v3#S6.SS2)
